items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1969-12-14
items.q: we want to wish a very happy birthday this morning to Joey Catalinato

ctx.x: there's a very, very interesting story behind Snoozer Quinn's rendition, and that was Snoozer's Wanderings. And I want Mr. Johnny Wiggs to tell us just how that record was recorded. Well, I hope we have time to start at the beginning. I met Snoozer when Peck Kelly sent for me. Peck Kelly was considered one of the greatest piano players that ever lived. And he was playing in Freeport, and they sent for me, and I pulled out my horn to play the dinner session. And it was a big band in those days. That was supposed…

slam the door in nurses' faces. It was done out at the hospital, the TB hospital out the lake. I had to slam the door in audits' faces. I had to take phones off of hooks and brush off the hair which is caused by these platter machines. And lo and behold, if we didn't get 12 of fairly good sides, which are on the market now. Okay, and we're going to be hearing some of those, but first we have to bring you this message. Hi, Karate, after Shaven. Cologne presents. All right, we want to wish a very happy birthday…

baby. That will be coming up shortly, but we want to go back to the multi-phones with another call here for you. Good morning. You're on the air with Dick Allen of Tulane University. And Mr. Johnny Wiggs. Yes, sir. Go ahead. This is Eddie Jazz. One of the original jazz man. See, I like to set the record straight about jazz. Jazz is only 55 years old. There's no such thing as jazz before that. And that was just what's going on now. Everybody is using one another's questions about jazz. Now, I'm related to Tom…
